Null intervals of the tests of each site

Source: R/trait_plots.R
null_intervals.Rd

Summarises, for each site, trait and statistic, the null distribution kept by tstats() or community_index(): its median, an outer interval (level) and an inner one (inner), with the observed value, the standardised effect size and the one-sided tests of tstats_summary(). This is the table drawn by the plot() methods of these objects, and can be used to build other figures.

Usage

null_intervals(x, level = 0.95, inner = 0.5)

Arguments

x

Result of tstats() or community_index() with n_perm > 0.

level

Coverage of the outer null interval, and 1 - level the size of the two-sided test that defines deviation.

inner

Coverage of the inner null interval.

Value

A data frame with one row per site, trait and statistic (for community_index(), statistic is the name of the index) and the columns observed, null_median, null_low, null_high, inner_low, inner_high, ses, p_low, p_high and deviation ("low", "high", "none" or NA for sites that cannot be tested).

See also

plot.tstats(), tstats_summary().

Other trait variation among individuals: community_index(), drift_test(), neighbour_metrics, nested_variance(), plot.mc_trait_gradient(), plot.nested_variance(), plot.trait_flex(), plot.trait_rarefaction(), plot.tstats(), plot_population_traits(), population_shifts(), sample_individuals(), subsample_individuals(), trait_densities(), trait_flex(), trait_gradient(), trait_gradient_bayes(), trait_gradient_phylo(), trait_gradient_test(), trait_gradient_weights(), trait_rarefaction(), tstats(), tstats_summary()

Examples

set.seed(1)
ind <- data.frame(site = rep(paste0("s", 1:6), each = 20),
                  species = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 120, replace = TRUE))
ind$trait <- c(a = 10, b = 20, c = 30)[ind$species] + rnorm(120)
head(null_intervals(tstats(ind, n_perm = 99)))
